title: SI Prefix and Scale Explorer
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Drag a marker along a scale spanning many powers of ten and read the same value three ways at once - plain decimal, scientific notation, and with its SI prefix - beside a familiar object of that size.

learningObjectives: Interpret a value written in scientific notation by connecting it to an SI prefix and to a familiar physical object at that scale.
Explain what one order of magnitude means in concrete terms.
prerequisites: Reading a number in scientific notation

keyQuestions: Why does the SI prefix change every three decades rather than every one?
Which is bigger: 5000 hPa or 0.5 MPa?
How many orders of magnitude separate a bacterium from a two-storey house?
commonMisconceptions: Treating "micro" as a vague word for "small" rather than as exactly 10^-6.
Assuming a value with a large-sounding prefix must be a large quantity, without checking the unit.
Reading 10^-9 as "nine times smaller" instead of "a billionth".
assessmentOpportunities: Given a value in scientific notation, states the matching SI prefix without consulting a table.
Explains "one order of magnitude" as a factor of ten rather than as "a lot".
Correctly identifies 101325 Pa as roughly 1013 hPa and recognises it as ordinary sea level pressure.
